core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 3229-3240): let B be the set of weakly contractible objects; every object T has a finite covering by members of B by the covering lemma, so the hypercovering lemma produces a hypercovering K of U whose degree n term consists of finitely many weakly contractible objects; replacing K by the hypercovering given by the disjoint unions of its terms puts it in the required single-object form.

Part (2) (proof lines 3242-3266): consider the full subcategory of quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of the pro-etale site with finite pro-etale coverings as its coverings; it is a site with fibre products and its inclusion into the pro-etale site is continuous and commutes with fibre products, so hypercoverings there are hypercoverings in the pro-etale site.

Apply the affine covering lemma inside the subcategory (proof lines 3256-3266): by the lemma producing weakly contractible affine coverings and the fact that finite unions of affines are affine, every object of the subcategory has a covering by a single affine weakly contractible object; the hypercovering lemma then gives a hypercovering with finitely many affine weakly contractible terms per degree, and taking degreewise disjoint unions gives the required single-object hypercovering.
proof_roadmap: Cover an arbitrary object by finitely many weakly contractible objects and apply the hypercovering construction.
Replace the hypercovering by its degreewise disjoint unions so that each term is a single object.
For quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects, run the same construction inside the subcategory of such objects and use affine weakly contractible coverings.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that every object of the pro-etale site of a scheme admits a hypercovering whose every term is a single weakly contractible object, and that a quasi-compact and quasi-separated object admits such a hypercovering with each term a single affine weakly contractible object (statement lines 3215-3227). The proof (proof lines 3229-3266) applies the hypercovering construction to finite coverings by weakly contractible objects, replaces hypercoverings by their degreewise disjoint unions, and repeats the argument inside the subcategory of quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects using affine weakly contractible coverings. H2: two parallel constructions with four inputs, written out in full.
